title: The company that bought the bank

probes.question: In the story, what happened to France's money supply as shareholders sold?
True or false: the Mississippi Company's first shares were offered at 500 livres, and later reached a peak of 10,000 livres.

image.alt: An 18th-century engraving of a dense crowd of traders in the Rue Quincampoix in Paris during the speculation of 1720.

panels.text: In 1717 the Scottish financier John Law founded a joint-stock company. Its first shares were offered at 500 livres.
In February 1720 the company acquired John Law's Bank, which had been France's first central bank.
Share prices eventually reached a peak of 10,000 livres. As shareholders sold, the money supply in France suddenly doubled and inflation burgeoned, reaching 23% in a single month in January 1720.
In the second half of 1720 the shares collapsed, an event called the Mississippi Bubble. By April 1721 the company was in government receivership.
